IE.title: Infective endocarditis (infection of the heart lining or valves)

items: Infective endocarditis is an infection of the inner lining of the heart, usually the valves.
It is serious and often needs hospital treatment for several weeks.
Prolonged fever, tiredness, and a new heart murmur (extra heart sound).
Small spots on the skin or under the nails, and small blood clots (emboli) that can affect the brain or limbs.
At least 3 sets of blood cultures from separate sites, taken before antibiotics.
Echocardiogram (heart ultrasound), a transoesophageal scan (TEE, a probe passed through the gullet) if the first scan is not clear.
ECG, blood count, inflammation markers, and kidney function.
Antibiotics are given into a vein for several weeks, chosen from the culture result.
Your team will decide if any procedure is needed.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Take all antibiotics as prescribed, and keep your dental care up to date.
Tell any doctor or dentist that you have had endocarditis before.
Regular checks of your heart and blood tests are needed after treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Weakness, numbness, or a drooping face (possible clot to the brain)
